gen_risks.description: Climate‑related floods, landslides and earthquakes could damage roads, tourism sites and halt visitor access.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply climate‑resilient designs (drainage, slope stabilization, flood‑proof structures); conduct hazard mapping; establish emergency response plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate hazards also pose a challenge for tourism… floods and resulting mudslides weaken transportation infrastructure, road closures impede access to tourism destinations.

gen_risks.description: GORE Arequipa's Project Implementation Unit lacks experience with World Bank‑financed projects, risking implementation quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide intensive capacity building via GFPP, retain experienced advisors, define clear TORs and onboarding schedule for PIU staff.
gen_risks.evidence: It does not have experience implementing WB‑financed projects, so capacity building and close supervision will be required.

gen_risks.description: Delayed recruitment of Financial Management staff may weaken fiduciary controls.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare TORs early, start recruitment before effectiveness, use interim FM specialists if needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Delayed recruitment of FM staff… FM staff shall be appointed within two months after effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Potential inaccuracies in accounting and financial reporting due to limited experience.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use the national accounting system (SIAF), conduct annual independent audits, and provide accounting training for PIU finance team.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential inaccuracies in accounting and financial reporting… the national accounting system (SIAF) will be used, supplemented by annual independent audits.

gen_risks.description: Historical delays in budget allocation and execution could postpone project activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Submit budget requests immediately after loan signing; set up joint monitoring with MEF; maintain a cash‑flow tracking dashboard.
gen_risks.evidence: In Peru, initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates...

gen_risks.description: Disbursements will be blocked until three Inter‑institutional Agreements are signed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize agreement negotiations before effective date; assign a liaison to municipalities; track signing status weekly.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawals shall be made... unless the Bank has received at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements...

gen_risks.description: Fragmented institutional landscape may impede coordinated decision‑making.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen steering and consultative committees; define clear decision‑making protocols; hold regular inter‑agency workshops.
gen_risks.evidence: Efficient budgeting and implementation... hindered by lack of coordination within a highly fragmented institutional landscape.

gen_risks.description: Project‑related grievances may remain unresolved, affecting community support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a transparent GRM, publicize contacts, train staff on resolution, and monitor the % of grievances closed.
gen_risks.evidence: percentage of project‑related grievances addressed by the PIU

gen_risks.description: Increasing political instability could disrupt project continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure high‑level political commitments via steering committee; embed mandates in legal agreements; maintain continuous stakeholder communication.
gen_risks.evidence: ...and increased political instability in recent years.

gen_risks.description: Failure to satisfy key implementation conditions (PIU creation, key staff, committees) could halt effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a condition‑compliance tracker; allocate resources to meet each condition before effectiveness date.
gen_risks.evidence: The PIU has been created and its Key Staff appointed in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank.

gen_risks.description: Road safety may remain inadequate, risking accidents given high local fatality rates.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate guardrails, signage, pedestrian crossings; conduct independent road‑safety audits; train local maintenance crews on safety standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Designs will adopt specifications that enhance road safety, given Arequipa's higher road fatality rate than national average.

gen_risks.description: Work in protected areas could breach environmental regulations without SERNANP coordination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage SERNANP early; obtain all environmental permits; follow ESMP guidelines; monitor compliance throughout construction.
gen_risks.evidence: Coordination with SERNANP … will be required for work in the Salinas and Aguada Blanca National Reserve.

gen_risks.description: Private investors may delay participation until visible infrastructure upgrades are completed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a clear investment pipeline; showcase pilot sites; offer PPP frameworks and Obras por Impuestos incentives.
gen_risks.evidence: private sector is willing to invest once they see that infrastructure and tourism offerings are upgraded.

gen_risks.description: Project relies on external technical assistance for disaster‑risk finance and public‑investment reforms; delays could affect timelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Transfer knowledge early to PIU; document TA processes; ensure internal capacity to continue work if external support lags.
gen_risks.evidence: leverages ongoing TA on Disaster Risk Finance, which is developing innovative insurance programs for public assets in high‑risk areas.

gen_risks.description: Long‑term road sustainability may be compromised without effective maintenance arrangements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set up a dedicated O&M fund; train local authorities on maintenance; embed maintenance contracts in procurement.
gen_risks.evidence: the project will ensure that, once roads are completed, maintenance arrangements are put in place to ensure sustainability of the investments.

gt_risks.description: Peru is in a period of substantial political uncertainty (low popular support for the executive and Congress, high political fragmentation); a new government assumes office July 2026 and regional elections are scheduled October 2026. Since GORE Arequipa (a regional government) is the implementing agency, regional government changes could slow implementation or shift priorities; high-level changes at MINCETUR could also affect oversight commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Focus on highly needed, consensus-driven investments; maintain buy-in and continuous dialogue with the tourism private sector; engage proactively with any new authorities on project opportunities; use implementation arrangements that are technically strong, highly competent, and relatively shielded from political influence and staff turnover.

gt_risks.description: Tourism projects are inherently complex, involving infrastructure, capacity building, and multiple government levels/sectors plus private-sector and community stakeholders. Capacity must be built at GORE Arequipa given no precedent for multisectoral regional investment programs in Peru, and historic national-regional coordination weaknesses. The project also does not budget for O&M of delivered sites/infrastructure, which falls to designated stakeholders.
gt_risks.mitigation: Institutional capacity building via the Project (incl. GFPP) to ready GORE for implementation; World Bank support on PIU composition and key staff selection; coordination arrangements/agreements between the PIU and local partners in charge of operating sites, to align on design, implementation, and handover.

gt_risks.description: Combined fiduciary risk with GORE Arequipa is Substantial, reflecting the entity's lack of prior experience with World Bank or other MDB-financed operations in both financial management and procurement.
gt_risks.mitigation: A fiduciary assessment identified capacity gaps and informed mitigation measures; recruit dedicated FM and Procurement Specialists supported by qualified administrative staff; detail minimum FM/procurement procedures aligned with WB requirements in the Project Operational Manual; use SIAF for financial transactions/reporting and STEP for procurement planning/monitoring; targeted WB training, regular fiduciary supervision, and annual audits.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk reflects the scope/nature of planned interventions, works located in environmentally and culturally sensitive areas, and GORE Arequipa's limited institutional capacity to manage risks per the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthen PIU capacity to manage E&S risks with adequate resources/staffing; elaborate and implement project-level instruments (Stakeholder Engagement Plan, Labor Management Plan, SEA/SH Plan) plus intervention-level instruments with specific mitigation measures.
